title: EV charging for apartment buildings and offices | VOOL
description: Charge more cars without upgrading the grid connection. Load management, billing per user and reports for the association.

sections.title: Charging for the whole building, on the connection you have
sections.lead: VOOL shares the building’s spare capacity between the cars. The association or the company runs charging itself, and only the people who charge pay for it.
sections.alt: VOOL charger at an apartment building

sections.title: Why associations and property managers choose VOOL

items.title: No grid upgrade
items.text: Automatic phase switching and load management make full use of the existing connection.

items.title: Fair costs
items.text: Each driver pays for their own charging. Owners without an electric car pay nothing.

items.title: No separate operator
items.text: The association manages users and billing in the VOOL Portal. We provide support and maintenance.

sections.title: Prepare now, expand later
sections.text: Mount casings on every parking space during the building work. Click in a charging controller when the owner of that space gets an electric car.

sections.title: Management that fits a board meeting

items.title: 45 chargers on 125 A
items.text: One tenant on a Luxembourg business campus runs 45 VOOL chargers on a single 125 A connection.

items.title: 19 chargers in three weeks
items.text: In a 74-space residence, owners ordered 19 chargers within three weeks of the shared installation.

items.title: Getting it through the meeting
items.text: A draft resolution, answers to owners’ questions and what the law says.

sections.title: What charging at home costs a driver
sections.lead: A number for the board to show owners.
sections.note: Example values for Estonia; enter your own. The electricity price should include energy, network fees and taxes. Assumes 18 kWh/100 km and 6.5 l/100 km.

sections.title: Who runs the charging? You choose.

items.title: The association runs it
items.text: VOOL provides the platform, billing and support. The board sets the price and sees the reports. No separate operator is needed.

items.title: An operator runs it
items.text: If the board wants no part in it, an operator partner owns or manages the chargers on VOOL.

items.title: Each owner buys a charger
items.text: The association builds the shared cabling and load management. Owners add their own charger when they need one.

items.title: You send the basics
items.text: Parking spaces, main fuse size and how many chargers you need now. A photo of the switchboard helps.

items.title: We size the system
items.text: VOOL works out how many chargers your connection carries with load management, and what to prepare for later.

items.title: A partner quotes and installs
items.text: VOOL does not install. A certified installation partner visits the site, quotes the work and builds it.

items.title: We set up the software
items.text: Users, prices and billing are set up in the VOOL Portal. Drivers charge with the VOOL App or an RFID card.

items.title: Support for the life of the system
items.text: Remote diagnostics, software updates and a 5-year warranty on the chargers.

sections.title: Who installs
sections.lead: VOOL makes the chargers, the load management and the software. Installation is done by local partners.

sections.title: Estonia: KIK pays part of the cost

items.title: €14,090 in grant for 10 charging points
items.text: Apartment associations outside Tallinn and Tartu city can apply for KIK’s EV charging grant. Load management is required, and VOOL LMC covers it.

sections.title: Tell us about your building
sections.lead: Number of parking spaces, main fuse size and how many chargers you need now. We reply within 1–2 working days.
